description: Generate realistic, graph-connected mock data from a GraphQL schema using faker, with a graph-backed request handler and Apollo link for answering any operation, plus a GraphQL Code Generator plugin that emits a SchemaTypeMap for typed mock pools.
rules: buildMocks(schema, options?) is the runtime entry point; it accepts a GraphQLSchema or an SDL string and returns a MockResult keyed by object-type name.

Relationships are wired as actual object references: todo.user is the same object as mocks.User[i], not a copy. Circular references resolve to already-generated objects, so a pool is not JSON-serializable.
Pools are unknown[] by default. Pass a TTypes map (buildMocks<{ User: User }>(schema)) or a generated SchemaTypeMap to get typed pools without a cast.

In overrides and derive the TTypes map is a hint, not a closed contract: type names are checked against it, but a field the map does not carry (one a fragment did not select, or a mock-only computed field) is accepted with an unknown return, and a derive's self stays typed. The trade is that a misspelled field name reads as an unmapped one. MockResult is unchanged: pooled instances are typed by the map alone.
Use the @vantreeseba/graphql-mocks-codegen plugin to auto-generate the SchemaTypeMap from a schema; run it alongside the standard typescript plugin in codegen.ts.
Determinism comes from the seed option; override and scalar functions receive the generator's seeded faker instance, so do not import a separate faker for them.

scalarFromPath('module.method', { args?, pick? }) builds a scalars entry from a dotted faker path, and buildScalarsFromPaths turns a whole registry ({ EmailAddress: 'internet.email', Slug: { path: 'lorem.slug', args: [2] } } or a [{ name, path }] list) into the scalars map. The path is typechecked against faker's real modules and methods, so no as-unknown-as cast is needed, and an unresolvable path throws from scalarFromPath() itself rather than mid-generation. The method is called on its module so faker keeps its this, the value is returned as faker produced it, and pick takes one property of an object-returning generator such as science.unit.

Default counts are 5 per type; every list field (scalar, enum, relationship and root) is sized by listSize (default 1-5), which accepts a flat number/range or a per-type/per-field map. Unknown scalars fall back to faker.lorem.word() with a console.warn.

Scalar and enum lists are drawn without replacement (uniqueLists, default true), like relationship lists, so their entries are distinct. The length gives way to that: a list of a three-value enum holds at most three entries whatever listSize says, and a generator with no more distinct values to give returns a short list (each slot re-draws at most 12 times). uniqueLists: false, or a map in the listSize shape ({ Post: { tags: false } }, resolved [type][field] -> [type]._default -> _default -> flat), restores repeats; a named entry outranks the catch-all. Under qa it defaults to false, since the QA corpora are too small to dedupe against.

Every object gets __typename by default (Apollo cache needs it); disable with addTypename: false. stableIds gives id fields readable TypeName-<index> values and every other string identifier field a TypeName-<field>-<index> value; identifier fields are recognized by name (id in any casing, or a name ending in Id/ID), and stableIds: ['code'] or { Currency: ['code'], _default: [] } adds the names the convention misses. Only string scalar singular fields are rewritten, and an explicit overrides entry still wins.

mocks.dataForOperation(document, variables?, matchArguments?) executes a query/mutation against the graph, returning data shaped to the selection set: root fields picked from pools by return type, nested fields follow wired refs, abstract fields resolve via __typename.

matchArguments is opt-in (default false) on buildMocks, a handler, or per call. It interprets only three buckets — equality against a same-named scalar/enum field, search args (search/query/q/filter/searchTerm/term or <field>Contains), and paging (skip/offset plus limit/first/take) — and ignores everything else. There is no fuzzy matching.

Arguments bound to variables the library auto-filled are ignored, so mockOperation(SomeByIdQuery) with no variables still returns a random pooled item. On a miss, lists return [], nullable singulars fall back to a random pick, and non-null singulars always fall back regardless of onMiss.

mocks.toRequestHandler(options?) answers any operation from the graph with no registration; results memoize per document+variables by default, overrides (matched by name, document identity, or predicate) force data/errors/networkError/loading/delay/once states, handler.calls records operations, and reset() clears memo, calls and consumed overrides. Mutations never mutate the pool.

mockLink(mocksOrHandler, options?) from @vantreeseba/graphql-mocks/apollo turns a graph or handler into an ApolloLink. @apollo/client is an optional peer (>=3.8 <5); the root entry has no Apollo dependency at all.

Apollo MockedProvider helpers build MockedResponse entries: the standalone mockOperation/mockOperationVariants take supplied data, while mocks.mockOperation/mocks.mockOperationVariants resolve data from the graph so the query's selection set picks the mocks.

mockOperation and mockOperationVariants also accept a resolver function of the variables, producing a DynamicMockedResponse with result as a function; the static overload is unchanged so result.data reads keep their types. The graph-bound forms take dynamic, transform and matchArguments options.

dataOf(mock, variables?) unwraps a mock envelope to its TData non-optionally, replacing mock.result?.data?.x ?? [] reads; it throws for the withError variant or an envelope without result/data, returns for withLongLoadTime, and passes variables (default {}) to a resolver-form result. dataForOperation is not idempotent — it re-resolves and draws from the shared seeded faker each call, so use dataOf to read what a built mock carries.

mockScenarios(base?, target?) returns default/loading/errored MockHandlerOptions; mocks.mockOperationsFrom(module) maps a codegen document module's export names to lazily built variants (withResults/withLongLoadTime/withError); paginate/searchItems are exported for wrapper types the argument engine cannot reach, and a searchItems field may be a key, a dotted path through relations (stepping through lists, missing link = non-match) or an accessor function.
mocks.ids(type), mocks.at(type, index) and mocks.byId(type, id) address pooled items directly; ids() types as string[] without a TTypes map.

Apollo helpers default to matching any variables with maxUsageCount Infinity (override via options.variables/delay/error/maxUsageCount). @graphql-typed-document-node/core is an optional peer for the TypedDocumentNode type.

fieldOverrides keys overrides by field name instead of by type, so one entry covers every mocked type carrying that field (imageUrl everywhere); a key wrapped in slashes is a regular expression ('/Url$/'). A type-keyed overrides entry wins, then an exact name, then patterns in declaration order; a key matching no field on any mocked type warns.

overrides functions run while an instance is half-built and cannot see sibling fields; derive functions run last — after scalars, overrides, relationship wiring and reciprocal mirroring — receive the finished object as self, and win over an overrides entry for the same field. Totals, assembled names and any value computed from the rest of the object belong in derive. FieldDeriveFn's self is bivariant, so a DeriveConfig<SchemaTypeMap> block (or one entry of it) declared away from the call is assignable to options that carry no type map, with no cast; return types stay checked against the map.

deriveObject ({ Type: (self, { index, typeName, faker }) => object }) is one function per type, run once per instance, returning a partial merged over the generated object — for fields that must come from a single correlated draw (subtotal/tax/total), which a per-field derive cannot express because each field takes the shared faker stream as it comes. It runs in the same phase as derive and sees the same finished object; within a type deriveObject runs first, so a derive for a key it returned wins and can read the correlated values off self. Both beat overrides. A key the returned object omits stays as generated, a nullish return leaves the instance untouched, and scenario layers merge it one level deep (per type, later function wins). ObjectDeriveConfig<TTypes> binds self to the owning type and a returned field the map carries to that field's type, while any other returned key is accepted.

aliases ({ Type: { field: name | [names] } }) also exposes a field under the name a fragment aliases it to, e.g. { User: { addresses: 'locations' } } for `locations: addresses`. The alias is the same reference, not a clone, and is applied after relationships, counts and derives; an unknown type or field, an operation or non-object type, or a collision with a real field throws.

relations shapes relationship fields after every pool exists: a number, a {min,max} range, null, 'all', a { size, where } filter, or (ctx) => value picking from ctx.pool. A { size, where } spec draws only from the pooled objects the where(item, ctx) predicate keeps, sized by size (any ordinary spec) or by the usual sizing when size is absent; a predicate matching nothing throws, a singular field cycles by the owner's index, and on a root field where narrows the pool that argument matching and paging then run against. It reaches root fields through the operation type ({ Query: { users: 3 } }), pools grow to meet demand, and { _reciprocal: true } (or 'hidden' for non-enumerable back-references) mirrors each reference into its inverse field.

countFields (boolean or { Type: { countField: listField } }) pairs a count scalar with the list it counts and sizes that list to the pool, so totalCount is a total of something a pager can page through. Pairing is by name (postCount/numberOfPosts/totalPosts -> posts; a nameless total/count/totalCount -> the type's single object list; Relay totalCount -> edges). relations sizing, an overrides entry for the count and a derive for the same field all still win; under a QA lists profile the profile owns the sizing and this only syncs counts. With matchArguments, a paired count on a wrapper type follows the narrowing: it reports the rows the filters left, before paging, while paging alone leaves it at the pool size.

paginateArgs(items, ctx, options) searches and pages a list straight from a field's arguments inside an argOverrides handler, returning { items, matchedCount, totalCount, skip, limit, search }. It reads the same argument names the matcher does — exported as DEFAULT_OFFSET_ARGS (skip/offset), DEFAULT_LIMIT_ARGS (limit/first/take) and DEFAULT_SEARCH_ARGS (search/query/q/filter/searchTerm/term) — and takes searchFields, offsetArgs, limitArgs, searchArgs, defaultLimit and flattenInputs. With no page size the result is unpaged, not empty. totalField: 'totalCount' stamps matchedCount onto every returned row under that name, for a flattened aggregate field that returns a bare list and repeats the page total on each row — the row-level counterpart to countFields; the stamped rows are shallow copies so the pooled objects keep their own values, an existing value under that name is overwritten, and a row that is not an object passes through.

Argument matching unwraps wrapper and connection types so arguments apply to the list inside them (unwrap, listPath), matches inside nested input objects, and turns an argument no bucket can interpret into a deterministic partition key so aliased selections of the same field return different rows (partition: false opts out). An empty list stays empty — nothing draws [] from a non-empty pool unless something asked for nothing, so qa: { lists: 'empty' } and relations: 0/null survive paging. argOverrides answers one field by its argument values while every other field still resolves from the graph.

Pooled objects are cyclic, so anything walking them generically (JSON.stringify, snapshots, deep equality, structuredClone) needs a guard: toPlain(value, options?) deep-copies and cuts cycles (onCycle 'stub'|'null'|'omit', maxDepth), and select(value, document) projects onto a document's selection set and is cycle-free by construction; toPlain returns the type it was given and select infers its result from a TypedDocumentNode. Data returned by dataForOperation or a request handler is already acyclic.

Apollo invokes result only when result itself is a function — a function at result.data is never called and fails silently. validateMocks/assertValidMocks check one mock, an array, a variants trio or a whole module namespace for that and the other quiet failures (unparsed query, missing result/error, functions inside data); both walks are cycle-safe, so a module may export a built pool alongside its mocks. Issues carry kind: 'invalid' for a real defect, or the single 'empty' report meaning nothing was found to check; a mockOperationsFrom map is walked like any other module and its lazy entries are forced, and allowEmpty: true drops the 'empty' report for a caller validating a glob.

containsMocks(value) answers whether a value holds at least one Apollo mock — the validateMocks walk, stopped at the first hit and cycle-safe the same way. It is what a glob's fixture-only modules are filtered out with before validating (modules.filter(containsMocks)), and what lets a test assert a floor so a broken glob cannot pass by asserting nothing. It builds nothing: a lazy mockOperationsFrom map is recognised by its brand and answered from its key list, never by reading an entry, unlike Object.values or a hand-rolled walk.

createMockClient(source, options?) from ./apollo builds a whole ApolloClient: mockLink plus a fresh InMemoryCache per call and fetchPolicy 'no-cache' / errorPolicy 'all' for query and watchQuery. defaultOptions is a deep partial merged per operation kind then per key, so { mutate: { errorPolicy: 'all' } } alone is valid. withGraphqlMocks(source, { wrap }) is the Storybook decorator over the same resolution, reading the graphqlMocks story parameter; pass a (options) => buildMocks(...) factory when stories need to rebuild the graph. Its client memo is keyed by story id and parameter, so a re-render reuses one client while two stories never share an InMemoryCache; clientKey: (context) => string opts a set of stories into one shared client.

toMockClientParameter(parameter) from ./apollo is the long form of any graphqlMocks story parameter, read exactly as the decorator reads it: an absent parameter and true are { state: 'default' }, a string is that state, a long form is copied through. withState(parameter, state) and withQa(parameter, qa) are built on it, parameter-in / parameter-out, and keep the base's overrides, target, build and handler options, so a derived story differs only in what it names; false (a story opted out of mocking) comes back as false. Re-stating a short form instead drops the base's overrides silently.

qa swaps generators for deliberately out-of-norm values across text, lists, nulls, numbers and dates; buildQaSets returns one pool per preset and buildMatrix crosses a scenarios map with QA presets. Scenarios are named partial BuildMocksOptions applied left to right with explicit options last, merging count per type and overrides/derive/relations/countFields two levels deep. defineScenarios<SchemaTypeMap>()({ ... }) binds the map while keeping literal keys, and composeScenarios<SchemaTypeMap>(a, b) checks every piece against it.

ESM-only, TypeScript 5 strict. Runtime peer deps: graphql >=16, @faker-js/faker >=9 (optional @graphql-typed-document-node/core >=3 and @apollo/client >=3.8 <5); codegen plugin also needs @graphql-codegen/plugin-helpers and visitor-plugin-common.
